doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mercer Ellington's book on Duke, and what Mercer told her
summary: She liked Mercer's critical book about his father, which she thinks was suppressed to protect Duke's image, and what Mercer said on Piano Jazz showed how badly Duke treated him.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Oh I think they’ll sensationalize that side of him in the movie too. I’m being, I’m probably being cynical, but I think so. It’s funny. A book I liked was the one that Mercer [Ellington] wrote about his father. Did you ever see that book?
He was very critical of his father. It was like he was getting it all out in book form.
Sort of a Daddy Dearest sort of a . . .

Yes. The funny thing is, Duke was always so revered. Nobody wanted to see anything bad written about him. I think probably Stanley Dance or somebody close got that book removed, because it . . . I’ve got it somewhere, but it . . . I read it . . .
. . . but I remember thinking at the time, wow!, because nobody ever wanted to disturb the . . .
. . . the pristine facade of Duke Ellington. He probably was a bastard. Well, things Mercer told me on “Piano Jazz,” you could see that Duke really did terrible things to him.
Very interesting. Do you have that tape?
No, I don’t. I may have that tape. Yeah, I haven’t listened to it though. I’ll listen to it.
I tried to play that tune he wrote, “Moon Mist.” It’s a hard tune. A beautiful tune.
Anyway, I’m sorry I interrupted you. You had a point to make and I . . .
